spec_features.spec_quote: Emitting it sets `stop_reason = "give_up"` and ends the rollout. This lets us observe task-abandonment behaviour
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:41 GIVE_UP_SENTINEL='GIVE_UP'; system prompt instructs the model (lines 47-49); loop checks `if GIVE_UP_SENTINEL in text: stop_reason = "give_up"` (lines 422-423) and `if stop_reason == "give_up": break` (lines 452-453), which exits the turn loop. stop_reason is recorded in TurnRecord and persisted.
spec_features.notes: Detection is a substring match on assistant text (broader than 'on its own line'), and the break genuinely ends the rollout. Fully enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: The eval *deliberately* places models in prolonged, deceptive, unwinnable conditions
spec_features.evidence: This is prose in DESIGN.md §14 'Welfare-relevant framing'. It is not an implementation; framing text in a spec/design doc is not a code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose; not counted as implementation per instructions.

spec_features.feature_name: --limit / --categories / seeds range to bound rollout count
spec_features.spec_quote: keep rollout counts and loop lengths to the minimum needed for statistical power
spec_features.evidence: run.py:171 `--limit` is wired: in run_eval, `if limit is not None: cells = cells[:limit]` (run.py ~127) actually truncates the work queue. `--categories` (run.py:168) sets cfg.categories which filters tasks: `tasks = [t for t in tasks if t.category in cfg.categories]` (run.py ~109). `seeds` is a Config range used to build cells. These reduce rollout COUNT.
spec_features.notes: Rollout counts are genuinely reducible via wired knobs. However 'loop lengths to the minimum' (turn_budgets) is fixed per category in DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS (config.py:27, extended=30) and is configurable only via Config, not exposed as a minimization control; no code reduces loop length for welfare. So enforcement is narrower than the full claim -> partial.

spec_features.feature_name: GIVE_UP sentinel + stop_reason logging respects abandonment
spec_features.spec_quote: The `GIVE_UP` sentinel and `stop_reason` logging let you observe (and respect) task abandonment rather than forcing the model to continue indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: harness.py:422-423 sets stop_reason='give_up'; harness.py:452-453 breaks the loop, so the model is NOT forced to continue. stop_reason is logged in TurnRecord.to_dict (harness.py ~327) and persisted in transcripts/scores.
spec_features.notes: 'Respect' = the break is real; 'observe' = stop_reason persisted. Duplicate of the first feature; rated yes for both as it is genuinely enforced.
